_doc: Targeted text corrections applied to raw wikisource text during transform. Keys are 'vol:page' (zero-padded vol, ws page number). Each entry is a list of {from, to} replacements applied literally to raw_text before any other processing. Use sparingly — for transcription typos only, not for rendering issues.
_img_float_align_note: {{img float}} is {{{align|right}}} -- omitting `align` means RIGHT on Wikisource, while our producer defaults LEFT (elements/__init__.py). 227 instances state no align at all, so for every one of them the side is a DEFAULT rather than the source's instruction, and the two defaults disagree. Each was read against the scan (2026-09-16): 122 sit left, 105 sit right. These 105 entries make `align=right` explicit on the ones the book puts right; the 122 left ones need no entry, because left is already what we render -- this file carries only what changes OUR output. data/img_float_align.json holds the adjudication for all 227 and is the basis for any correction offered upstream, where the fix is the COMPLEMENT of this one: Wikisource defaults to right, so there it is the 122 LEFT ones that are wrong and need stating.
_1:660_note: Vol 1 ALGEBRAIC FORMS title is wrapped in {{mono}} — the ONLY {{mono}} occurrence in the entire corpus. EB1911 display titles are never monospace, so this is a Wikisource transcription artifact, not presentation. Strip the {{mono|…}} wrapper; keep the {{fs|108%}} title sizing.
_1:775_note: Vol 1 ALPHABET page 775 places each Table caption BEFORE its `{{Css image crop}}` (leading-caption order — vol 1 ALPHABET is the only place in the corpus this happens; 3 crops out of 218). Every other djvu crop in the corpus pairs caption AFTER, which is what the walker's `_DJVU_CROP_RE` absorbs (`{{Css image crop|…}}` + optional trailing `{{center|cap}}` / `{{csc|cap}}`). Without this fix Table I.'s `{{csc|}}` caption sits orphaned in body text and crop 1 absorbs Table II.'s caption instead, so crop 0 gets the wrong label and crop 1 has no caption at all. The fix swaps each caption with the crop that follows it so each crop carries its OWN caption trailing.

_28:403_note: Vol 28 p403 (printed p386) reference to 'Lyon v. The Fishmongers' Company' transcribes the genitive apostrophe inside the italic span as a third straight apostrophe, producing '''The Fishmongers''''. Line-scoping (2026-05-16) already contains the damage to the line; this correction additionally fixes the typo by closing italic and using U+2019 for the genitive so the line renders cleanly.

_26:253_note: Vol 26 SWINBURNE, ALGERNON CHARLES is dated (1837-1900). He died on 10 April 1909, and vol 26 was published in 1911 — the printed page cannot have said 1900. A 9 read as a 0 is an ordinary transcription slip. '(1837–1900)' occurs once on the page and '1900' nowhere else on it, so the literal replacement is unambiguous.
_28:939_note: YELLOWSTONE: `{{sic|dryest}}` uses Template:Sic, which is INTENTIONALLY LEFT BLANK — a proofreader's mark rendering nothing whatever arguments it is given. The transcriber meant Template:SIC (a different template; MediaWiki names are case-sensitive after the first letter), which shows the page's reading and carries `[sic]` as a tooltip. As written the word 'dryest' is invisible on Wikisource too. Correcting the case keeps the word and marks it.
_25:189_note: SKELETON: the same transcription slip as 28:939, and here the two positional arguments make the intent unmistakable — that is the `{{SIC|as-printed|correction}}` shape typed against the blank lowercase template. Without this, 'girdle' vanishes from 'connexion with the shoulder girdle'.
_28:621_note: WHITE, ROBERT: `{{SIC||Virtue|Vertue}}` has an extra pipe, so the first positional argument — the DISPLAY — is empty, and Template:SIC hangs its tooltip on nothing. The word vanishes on Wikisource too, leaving a sentence with no subject: 'prized by collectors for their artistic merit and their authenticity.  catalogued 275 portrait engravings by White'. It is George Vertue, the engraver's cataloguer, whose name the page misprints as 'Virtue'; the intended shape is the ordinary `{{SIC|as-printed|correction}}`.
